blocks.content: This chapter covers Meghalaya-specific development initiatives and its tourism circuit, which draws heavily on the natural and cultural landmarks already introduced in earlier chapters.

items: Central flagship schemes (Ayushman Bharat, PM Awas Yojana, Jal Jeevan Mission, PM-KISAN) have been extended to Meghalaya, alongside state-specific initiatives.

Meghalaya has positioned itself as a pioneer in community-led rural development, with programmes channelling funds directly through traditional village institutions (Dorbar Shnong and similar customary bodies) in partnership with the state government — an approach that leverages the state's strong existing tradition of community self-governance (Chapter 2).

Given its promotion as an eco-tourism and organic-farming hub (Chapters 6, 9), the state has emphasised sustainable-tourism infrastructure investment, including initiatives to formally recognise and support community-managed conservation areas and rural homestay networks in root-bridge and cave-tourism villages.

cells: State capital; 'Rock Capital of India'; Ward's Lake, Shillong Peak, Elephant Falls
World rainfall records (Chapter 1); waterfalls (Nohkalikai Falls, among India's tallest plunge waterfalls); limestone caves
Double-Decker root bridge and other living root bridges (Chapter 1); trekking destination
Border town near Bangladesh, famous for the exceptionally clear waters of the Umngot River, popular for boating
A village widely publicised as one of Asia's/India's cleanest villages, promoted as a community-led eco-tourism model

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Mawlynnong's reputation as one of 'Asia's cleanest villages' (a title popularised by Discover India magazine and widely repeated since) and Dawki's crystal-clear Umngot River are two of the most frequently tested modern tourism-branding facts for Meghalaya.

items: Meghalaya channels rural development funds through traditional village institutions (Dorbar Shnong) — a distinctive community-led governance approach.

Shillong ('Rock Capital of India'), Cherrapunji/Mawsynram (rainfall records), Nongriat (living root bridges), Dawki (Umngot River), Mawlynnong ('cleanest village') are the flagship tourism destinations.
Nohkalikai Falls (near Cherrapunji) is among India's tallest plunge waterfalls.
